symptom_text: runny nose sneezing sore throat mild cough nasal congestion low grade fever watery eyes mild body ache
description: A mild viral infection of the upper respiratory tract. It is self-limiting and usually resolves within a week with rest and fluids.
precautions: Use steam inhalation to relieve congestion
Avoid close contact to prevent spreading
Use saline nasal drops if needed
diet: Warm fluids like soups and herbal teas, citrus fruits for vitamin C, ginger and honey, and light easily digestible meals.

symptom_text: high fever body ache chills fatigue dry cough headache sore throat severe weakness sweating
description: A contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. Symptoms are more severe than a common cold and come on suddenly.
precautions: Take antipyretics for fever such as paracetamol
Consult a doctor if fever exceeds 3 days
diet: Plenty of fluids, broths and soups, soft foods, fruits rich in vitamin C, and avoid heavy oily food until recovery.

symptom_text: high fever severe headache pain behind the eyes joint pain muscle pain skin rash nausea vomiting bleeding gums fatigue
description: A mosquito-borne viral infection common in tropical regions. It can progress to severe dengue, which is a medical emergency.
precautions: Seek medical care and monitor platelet count
Stay well hydrated with fluids and ORS
Take only paracetamol, avoid aspirin and ibuprofen
Watch for warning signs like bleeding
diet: Papaya leaf extract (traditionally used), coconut water and ORS for hydration, soft protein-rich foods, and iron-rich foods to support platelets.

symptom_text: cyclical fever with chills profuse sweating headache nausea vomiting muscle pain fatigue shivering shaking
description: A mosquito-borne disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, characterised by cyclical episodes of fever, chills and sweating.
precautions: Get a blood test for malaria parasites promptly
Complete the full course of prescribed antimalarials
Seek urgent care if confusion or breathlessness occurs
diet: Plenty of fluids, glucose and fruit juices for energy, easily digestible carbohydrates, and vitamin-rich fruits and vegetables.

symptom_text: fever dry cough loss of smell loss of taste fatigue shortness of breath sore throat body ache headache congestion
description: A respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Severity ranges from mild cold-like symptoms to serious breathing difficulty.
precautions: Monitor oxygen saturation with a pulse oximeter
Seek care if breathing becomes difficult
diet: Warm fluids, protein-rich foods for recovery, vitamin C and D sources, zinc-rich foods, and plenty of water.

symptom_text: throbbing headache on one side of the head nausea sensitivity to light sensitivity to sound aura visual disturbance dizziness
description: A neurological condition causing intense, often one-sided throbbing headaches, frequently accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light and sound.
precautions: Rest in a quiet, dark room
diet: Regular balanced meals, avoid known triggers like aged cheese, caffeine and processed meats, magnesium-rich foods, and stay well hydrated.

symptom_text: dull aching headache pressure or tight band around the head tight neck and shoulder muscles mild pain on both sides scalp tenderness stress
description: The most common type of headache, caused by muscle tension, stress or poor posture. It feels like a tight band around the head.
precautions: Use over the counter pain relief sparingly
diet: Balanced regular meals, adequate hydration, limit caffeine and alcohol, and magnesium-rich foods like nuts and leafy greens.

symptom_text: watery diarrhea vomiting abdominal cramps nausea low grade fever loss of appetite dehydration stomach pain
description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, usually from a viral or bacterial infection, leading to diarrhoea and vomiting.
precautions: Avoid dairy and oily food temporarily
diet: ORS and clear fluids, the BRAT diet of banana, rice, applesauce and toast, and avoid spicy, oily and dairy foods.

symptom_text: sudden nausea vomiting diarrhea abdominal pain cramps fever weakness after eating contaminated food dehydration
description: Illness caused by eating contaminated food, producing rapid onset of nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea, usually within hours of eating.
precautions: Stay hydrated with ORS and clear fluids
Rest and let the stomach settle
Avoid solid food until vomiting stops
Do not take anti-diarrhoeal drugs without advice
See a doctor if symptoms are severe
diet: Clear fluids and ORS first, then bland foods like toast, rice and bananas, and avoid dairy, caffeine and fatty foods.

symptom_text: burning sensation during urination frequent urination cloudy or bloody urine pelvic pain strong smelling urine urgency lower abdominal discomfort
description: An infection in any part of the urinary system, most often the bladder, causing burning and frequent urination.
precautions: Do not hold urine for long
Complete the full antibiotic course if prescribed
Consult a doctor for a urine test
diet: Plenty of water, cranberry juice (unsweetened), vitamin C rich foods, and avoid caffeine, alcohol and spicy foods that irritate the bladder.

symptom_text: persistent headache dizziness blurred vision chest discomfort shortness of breath occasional nosebleeds fatigue high blood pressure readings
description: A chronic condition where blood pressure against artery walls is persistently high, increasing risk of heart disease and stroke.
diet: Low sodium DASH diet, potassium-rich fruits and vegetables, whole grains, limit processed and fried foods, and reduce caffeine.

symptom_text: excessive thirst frequent urination increased hunger fatigue blurred vision slow healing wounds unexplained weight loss tingling in hands and feet
description: A metabolic disorder where the body cannot use insulin effectively, leading to high blood sugar over time.
precautions: Maintain a low sugar balanced diet
diet: Complex carbohydrates and whole grains, high fibre vegetables, lean protein, limit sugar and refined carbs, and controlled portion sizes.

symptom_text: wheezing shortness of breath chest tightness persistent cough difficulty breathing especially at night breathlessness on exertion triggered by allergens
description: A chronic condition where the airways narrow and swell, producing wheezing, breathlessness and coughing.
precautions: Seek emergency care for severe attacks
diet: Anti-inflammatory foods, fruits and vegetables rich in antioxidants, omega-3 sources, and avoid known food triggers and sulphites.

symptom_text: high fever productive cough with phlegm chest pain when breathing shortness of breath chills fatigue rapid breathing sweating
description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in the lungs, which may fill with fluid, causing cough, fever and breathing difficulty.
precautions: Get a chest X-ray if advised
diet: Plenty of fluids, protein for tissue repair, vitamin C and A rich foods, warm soups, and easy to digest meals.

symptom_text: persistent cough producing mucus fatigue mild fever chest discomfort wheezing sore throat shortness of breath
description: Inflammation of the bronchial tubes that carry air to the lungs, usually causing a persistent cough with mucus.
precautions: Use a humidifier to ease breathing
See a doctor if cough persists beyond three weeks
diet: Warm fluids and soups, honey and ginger for the throat, vitamin C rich fruits, and avoid dairy if it thickens mucus.

symptom_text: facial pain and pressure nasal congestion thick nasal discharge reduced sense of smell headache post nasal drip pressure around the eyes and cheeks
description: Inflammation of the sinuses, often following a cold, causing facial pressure, congestion and thick nasal discharge.
precautions: Use steam inhalation and saline rinses
Apply warm compresses to the face
Consult a doctor if symptoms last over 10 days
diet: Warm fluids, spicy foods to clear congestion, vitamin C rich foods, and avoid dairy and cold foods that increase mucus.

symptom_text: persistent fatigue weakness pale skin shortness of breath dizziness cold hands and feet brittle nails rapid heartbeat headache
description: A condition where there are not enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen, most often due to iron deficiency.
precautions: Get a blood test to confirm and find the cause
Pair iron with vitamin C for absorption
diet: Iron-rich foods like leafy greens, beans, red meat and fortified cereals, vitamin C to aid absorption, and avoid tea or coffee with meals.

symptom_text: persistent fatigue unexplained weight gain intolerance to cold dry skin hair loss constipation low mood depression slow heart rate puffy face
description: An underactive thyroid gland that does not produce enough thyroid hormone, slowing metabolism and causing fatigue and weight gain.
precautions: Take thyroid medication as prescribed at the same time daily
diet: Iodine and selenium sources, whole foods, adequate fibre for constipation, and limit heavily processed and goitrogenic foods in excess.

symptom_text: burning heartburn acid regurgitation chest discomfort after eating difficulty swallowing sour taste in mouth frequent burping throat irritation worse when lying down
description: A digestive disorder where stomach acid flows back into the food pipe, causing heartburn and regurgitation.
precautions: Do not lie down right after eating
diet: Small frequent meals, high fibre foods, non-citrus fruits and vegetables, and avoid spicy, fatty, caffeinated and acidic foods.

symptom_text: itchy rash with fluid filled blisters spreading across the body fever fatigue loss of appetite headache red spots turning into scabs
description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy blister-like rash along with fever and fatigue.
precautions: Keep nails trimmed and skin clean
diet: Soft bland foods, cool fluids, avoid salty and acidic foods that irritate mouth sores, and vitamin rich soft fruits.

symptom_text: prolonged stepwise fever abdominal pain weakness headache loss of appetite constipation or diarrhea rose colored spots on the abdomen fatigue
description: A bacterial infection from contaminated food or water, causing a sustained high fever, abdominal pain and weakness.
precautions: Get a blood test and start prescribed antibiotics
diet: High calorie soft foods, plenty of fluids and ORS, boiled and easily digestible foods, and avoid high fibre and spicy foods during illness.

symptom_text: red or pink eyes itchy eyes watery or sticky discharge gritty feeling in the eye swelling of the eyelids crusting of the eyelids in the morning
description: Inflammation of the transparent membrane covering the eye, commonly from a viral, bacterial or allergic cause.
precautions: Avoid touching or rubbing the eyes
Do not share towels or eye makeup
Apply a clean warm or cool compress
diet: Vitamin A and C rich foods for eye health, plenty of water, leafy greens and colourful vegetables, and omega-3 sources.

symptom_text: frequent sneezing itchy nose runny nose nasal congestion watery and itchy eyes itchy throat post nasal drip triggered by allergens like dust or pollen
description: An allergic reaction causing sneezing, a runny or blocked nose and itchy eyes when exposed to allergens like dust or pollen.
precautions: Keep windows closed during high pollen days
diet: Anti-inflammatory foods, vitamin C rich fruits, local honey (traditionally used), omega-3 sources, and stay well hydrated.

symptom_text: spinning sensation dizziness loss of balance nausea vomiting unsteadiness lightheadedness worsened by head movement
description: A sensation that you or your surroundings are spinning, often due to inner ear problems affecting balance.
precautions: Move slowly and avoid sudden head movements
Sit or lie down when dizzy
See a doctor to identify the cause
diet: Reduce salt intake, stay hydrated, limit caffeine and alcohol, and eat regular balanced meals to avoid low blood sugar.
